  "situation": "The National Intelligence Authority oversaw the Central Intelligence Group. It was considering how to assign the Group foreign-intelligence responsibilities under the presidential charter. Some national-security analysis fields were not being performed or were not being performed adequately. The Authority considered central coordination for foreign-intelligence work, while Cabinet departments retained limited analytical capabilities. The Army also maintained that the directive's wording preserved its Intelligence Division's independent collection operations.",
  "question": "What should the National Intelligence Authority do in allocating foreign-intelligence responsibilities between the Group and the Cabinet departments?",
  "facts": [
    {
      "id": "F1",
      "kind": "authority",
      "status": "confirmed",
      "fact": "The National Intelligence Authority oversaw the Central Intelligence Group and comprised the Secretaries of State, War, and Navy, with the President's chief military adviser.",
      "spans": ["src:9bbd203f49b6#p12.7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "F2",
      "kind": "authority",
      "status": "confirmed",
      "fact": "National Intelligence Authority Directive 5, issued on 8 July 1946, provided the Director of Central Intelligence with an implementation plan for the powers in the presidential charter for the Group.",

    },
    {
      "id": "F3",
      "kind": "capability",

    },
    {
      "id": "F4",
      "kind": "authority",
      "status": "confirmed",
      "fact": "The directive required the Director of Central Intelligence to coordinate all United States foreign-intelligence activities to implement the Authority's policies and objectives.",

    {
      "id": "F6",
      "kind": "intelligence",

      "fact": "The Authority assessed that many foreign-intelligence missions could be accomplished more efficiently centrally.",

    {
      "id": "F7",
      "kind": "capability",

    {
      "id": "F8",
      "kind": "situation",
      "status": "assessed",
      "fact": "The Authority's authorization was carefully phrased to allay departmental fears that the Director of Central Intelligence would take control of departmental intelligence offices, whose limited analytical capabilities the departments were unwilling to subordinate.",

    },

      "id": "F9",
